title: How Evaluation Protocol Shapes Reported Performance in CRISPR Guide-Efficiency Prediction
content: Background. Reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) in CRISPR guide-efficiency prediction depends on the binarisation threshold, the excluded fraction and the splitting unit. Both phenomena measured here have established names: spectrum bias, and type 1 and 2 circularity. We make no claim about how often these choices are reported. Three attempts to measure a reporting rate (Section 4.1) produced no defensible rate. Methods. For the protocol ladder we held one fixed model specification and one frozen out-of-fold prediction vector, assembled from five gene-grouped fold fits over 18,363 CRISPRi guides, and varied only the evaluation protocol. The comparisons across predictors, fold assignments and splits refit the models they name. Results. The reference span is 0.149 (0.137, 0.161): AUROC rises from 0.780 at the median split to 0.929 (top versus bottom 5%, 90% discarded). Under 40 alternative gene-to-fold assignments the mean 90%-cap AUROC is 0.926 and the mean span 0.147, and the deposited values exceed those of 37 of the 40, so the third decimal of the upper rungs is specific to the one deposited assignment. A Gaussian copula anchored to each predictor's median-split AUROC overshoots its protocol span by 37% to 63%, and every predictor's interval on that ratio excludes one. We tested only the Gaussian family. The margin between the linear baseline and the sequence-only boosted model falls from 0.014 at the median split to 0.003 at the 90% cap, not separable from zero from the 60% cap on, an observation we did not test against the copula's prediction. Per-gene conformal coverage is not distinguishable from calibration in aggregate, yet rises with guide count. Conclusions. Reported performance here is jointly determined by predictor and protocol. We release CRISPR-SCALE, an evaluation baseline under a fixed, fully stated protocol, reproducible within its pinned environment (Section 5).
